findings.description: The site footer copyright notice is left entirely in English on the French pages (shared footer, seen on the homepage).

Transaction dates on the French dashboard are rendered in US MM/DD/YYYY format (e.g. 09/15/2026), while the English version correctly uses ISO YYYY-MM-DD. This is not a valid fr-CA date format and is ambiguous/wrong (all three rows affected).
The "Recent transactions" section heading on the French dashboard is left untranslated in English, even though the summary card above it uses "opérations récentes".

findings.expected: Link should point to /fr/calculator on the French dashboard.
findings.description: On the French dashboard, the "Estimer un nouveau prêt" link points to the English calculator page (/en/calculator) instead of /fr/calculator, dropping the user out of the French locale.
"Balance" is an anglicism in fr-CA banking terminology; the standard term is "solde".

The validation error for the "Nom complet" field on the French loan application form is shown in English ("This field is required."), while all other field errors on the same form are correctly translated to "Ce champ est obligatoire."

findings.observed: Merci. Votre demande pour {montant} a été reçue.
findings.expected: Merci. Votre demande pour 15 000,00 $ a été reçue.
findings.description: The confirmation message on the French application summary page shows the raw unsubstituted template token "{montant}" instead of the formatted loan amount, while the English version correctly interpolates the value.

The checkbox labelled "Pay later" (name="pay_later", with help text "First payment deferred by 30 days") is translated as "Payer maintenant" (Pay now) in French — the opposite meaning, which could mislead a user about deferring their first payment.

findings.observed: Aucune accusation pour un remboursement anticipé.
findings.expected: Aucuns frais ne s'appliquent en cas de remboursement anticipé.
findings.description: "Accusation" is a mistranslation of "charges" in this financial context; in French "accusation" means a legal accusation, not a fee. The correct term is "frais".

findings.expected: Taux variable de 5,2 %, sous réserve d'approbation de crédit.
findings.description: The French rate disclaimer drops the "subject to credit approval" qualifier that is present in the English version, changing the meaning of the disclosure.

The estimated monthly payment on the French calculator page is shown in US currency format ($450.91) instead of Canadian French format (450,91 $), unlike the application summary page which correctly uses "15 000,00 $".
The modal's "Close" button is mistranslated as "Proche" (an adjective meaning "nearby/close by") instead of the verb "Fermer" (to close). A French user would not understand this as a close action.

findings.expected: Use a French version of the same promo image reading "Taux variable : 5,2 %" to match the alt text and the surrounding page content.
findings.description: The promotional banner image on the French calculator page uses a different file (promo-c.png) whose baked-in text reads "Taux fixe : 4,9 %" (Fixed rate: 4.9%), contradicting both its own alt text ("Taux variable : 5,2 %") and the page's variable-rate disclosure of 5.2%. The English page correctly shows a matching "Variable rate: 5.2%" image.

The homepage subtitle uses the informal "tu" register ("Découvre tes...") while the rest of the site (forms, error messages such as "Vous devez donner votre accord...") consistently uses the formal "vous" register. This is inconsistent for a banking site.

findings.observed: Financing that fits your plans / Competitive rates. Clear terms. No surprises. (baked into image src=/static/img/banner-en.png)
findings.expected: Use a French version of the banner image with text such as "Un financement qui correspond à vos projets. Taux concurrentiels. Conditions claires. Aucune surprise."
findings.description: The homepage banner image on the French page (/fr/) is the same English file (banner-en.png) as on the English page and displays untranslated English text baked into the graphic ("Financing that fits your plans", "Competitive rates. Clear terms. No surprises."), even though the image's alt attribute is correctly translated.

"Appliquer pour" is an anglicism in fr-CA (calque of "to apply for"); the standard term, correctly used elsewhere on the site (e.g. "Faites votre demande dès maintenant" on the calculator page), is "faire une demande".

findings.expected: Remove the fixed-width "btn-compact" class (or widen the button) so the longer French label wraps or fits, e.g. allow white-space: normal like the English button.
findings.description: The loan application submit button on the French page has a "btn-compact" class with a fixed width (210px) and white-space:nowrap, causing the longer French label "Soumettre ma demande de prêt" to be clipped (scrollWidth 290 > clientWidth 210); it visually reads "Soumettre ma demande". The English button uses no such compact class and displays fully.
